items.title: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab
items.description: The Somali government’s battle with Al-Shabaab militants grinds on, with neither able to gain a decisive advantage. To improve its lot, Mogadishu needs to bolster its military and alleviate civilian suffering in areas under insurgent control, while looking for openings for dialogue with the group.
items.titleIt: New Chapter, Same Stalemate: Somalia’s War with Al-Shabaab

items.title: “Strategic Balance” under Stress: Egypt and the U.S.-Israeli War with Iran
items.description: Egypt has been walking a tightrope since the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran began, joining mediation efforts while signalling solidarity with Gulf Arab partners under Iranian attack. But with some Gulf capitals voicing expectations of stronger support, Cairo may find itself under increasing pressure.

items.title: Sudan: UN Human Rights Council Urged to Widen Sudan Arms Embargo and Extend Fact-Finding Mission
items.description: [Dabanga] Geneva / Amsterdam -- The UN's Sudan fact-finding mission has urged the Human Rights Council to expand the Darfur arms embargo to the whole country, warning that foreign support is sustaining a war in which both sides may have committed war crimes. Sudan's government, however, rejects efforts to treat the warring parties as equivalent and says the conflict is being prolonged by external backing for the Rapid Support Forces.
items.titleIt: Sudan: UN Human Rights Council Urged to Widen Sudan Arms Embargo and Extend Fact-Finding Mission

items.title: Mattarella and Estonian counterpart Karis confirm support for Kyiv
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, 07 SET - President Sergio Mattarella met his Estonian counterpart Alar Karis at the Quirinal Palace in Rome on Monday in a meeting in which the two heads of State confirmed their support for Ukraine. The leaders also expressed the hope that "the ongoing negotiations will bring results". The two presidents discussed European integration, defence, Gaza, Israel and migration too. (ANSA). items.title: Meloni govt to extend 17-cent cut in diesel duties to Sept 10
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, 04 SET - The economy ministry has prepared a decree extending a 17-cent cut in diesel duties until September 10, sources said on Friday. The cut was first introduced by Premier Giorgia Meloni's government at the end of July to help people cope with high fuel costs following the return of conflict in the Persian Gulf and it has been renewed several times since. The current reduction was set to expire on Saturday. The cut, which does not regard unleaded petrol, has not stopped diesel prices from rising well above two euros a litre. The centre-left opposition has criticised the cut
items.titleIt: Meloni govt to extend 17-cent cut in diesel duties to Sept 10
